questions.text: Among three circles, the biggest circle's radius is 4 unit and medium circle's radius is 2 unit. A straight line is tangent to all three circles. Each circle touches the other two circles externally. What is the radius of the third circle?

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: A tunnel has the shape of a semi-ellipse that is $15 \mathrm{ft}$ high at the center, and $36 \mathrm{ft}$ across the base. What is the maximum height of a $12 \mathrm{ft}$ wide truck that can pass through the tunnel?

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: Two forces of 4 and $5 \mathrm{~kg}$-wt acting parallel to the length and base of a frictionless inclined plane, respectively, can singly support an object of weight on the plane. Find the value of $w$.

questions.subject: higher-math
questions.text: A heavy uniform rod balances about a fulcrum placed at a distance $c$ from one end when a weight $P$ is suspended from that end. When the weight $P$ is replaced by weight $Q$, the rod balances about a fulcrum placed at a distance $d$ from the same end. Show that the weight of the rod is $\frac{P c-Q d}{d-c}$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A boat with a velocity, $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{b}}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ started to move in a river of $36 \mathrm{~m}$ width from point $\mathbf{A}$ (Fig-1). The boat crossed the river and reached other side of the river at point $\mathrm{C}$ as shown in fig. Find the distance $\mathrm{BC}$ if the velocity of current $v_{r}=3 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. Also, find the angle with the direction of current at which the boat has to start in order to directly reach point $B$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A rock of mass $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ was initially at rest. It exploded and broke into three pieces of masses in the ratio $1: 1: 3$. The two pieces of equal masses moved perpendicular to each other with a speed of $18 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ each. What was the velocity of the heavier piece?

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The radius of a circular turn of a railroad is $500 \mathrm{~m}$ and the distance between the two rails is $1 \mathrm{~m}$. How much higher the outer rail has to be over the inner rail for banking needed for a train running at $54 \mathrm{kmh}^{-1}$ ?

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The human heart discharges $75 \mathrm{cc}$ of blood at each beat against an average pressure of $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ of mercury. Calculate the power of heart for the pulse frequency of 80 (eighty) per minutes. Density of mercury is $13.6 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cc}$.

questions.text:

$\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B} \xrightarrow[30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}]{\text { Zymaze }} \mathrm{X}+\mathrm{Y}$
$\mathrm{X}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \xrightarrow{\text { Acetobacter }} \mathrm{Z}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}$

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text: Two unlabeled aqueous solutions of $\mathrm{Zn}^{++}$and $\mathrm{Ca}^{++}$are present in a laboratory. How can the solutions be identified by using at most two reagents that are basic in nature? Show with reactions.

Find out the $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ of the reaction. $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~N}_{2}+\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{H}_{2} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_{3}$

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text:
$\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ is a common impurity in natural gases from different sources. The following reaction is used to remove $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ from natural gases:
$2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}(\mathrm{~g})+\mathrm{SO}_{2}(\mathrm{~g}) \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{~S}(\mathrm{~s})+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})$

In a typical process, if 10 liter of $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ at 0.95 atm and $290 \mathrm{~K}$ reacts with excess $\mathrm{SO}_{2}$, calculate the mass of $S$ produced as by-product.

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.text:
Lithium ion battery is one of the promising energy storage systems at present. The standard electromotive force of the battery is $3.70 \mathrm{~V}$. The cell reaction is as follows:
$\mathrm{CoO}_{2}+\mathrm{LiC}_{6} \rightarrow \mathrm{LiCoO}_{2}+6 \mathrm{C}$
(i) Write down the half-cell reactions of the battery.
(ii) Calculate the free energy change to show that the cell reaction of the battery is spontaneous.
